title: Blocks Whose Sum Is a Multiple of k

concept.title: Equal remainders of prefix sums
body: The block between two prefixes has the sum `prefix[j] - prefix[i]`. That difference is a multiple of `k` exactly when the two prefix sums leave the **same remainder** when divided by `k`. So count how often each remainder has occurred; every earlier prefix with the same remainder is the start of a good block.

body.code:
count = {0: 1}
prefix = total = 0
for x in a:
    prefix += x
    r = prefix % k
    total += count.get(r, 0)
    count[r] = count.get(r, 0) + 1

body: Careful with negative numbers: in C++ and Java `%` can give a negative remainder. Normalise it into `0..k-1` with `((prefix % k) + k) % k` (Java: `Math.floorMod`). Python already returns a non-negative remainder.

statement: Given an array of `n` integers (possibly negative) and a number `k`, count the blocks of consecutive elements whose sum is divisible by `k` (a sum of 0 is divisible).
hints: A block sum is a difference of two prefix sums.
The difference is divisible by k when both have the same remainder.
Count the remainders; make negative remainders non-negative.

explanation: Two prefix sums with the same remainder modulo `k` enclose a block whose sum is divisible by `k`. The map counts the remainders seen so far.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(min(n, k)).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

count = {0: 1}
prefix = 0
total = 0
for x in a:
    prefix += x
    rem = prefix % k
    total += count.get(rem, 0)
    count[rem] = count.get(rem, 0) + 1
print(total)
